units.text: In nineteen eighty-three, deep beneath an underground bunker, an old man lay strapped to a metal table in total silence.
Every sensory nerve in his body had been surgically cut.
The scientists believed that without the five senses, human thought could reach the pure presence of God.
Instead, something far darker found him in the void: hundreds of dead voices that refused to leave him alone.
And before his heart stopped forever, he delivered one final message.
Let us go back to the beginning.
A team of deeply religious scientists had theorized that physical senses cloud our awareness of eternity.
They believed that without stimuli, a person could touch the divine.
An elderly volunteer with nothing left to live for agreed to the radical surgery.
Surgeons severed every sensory nerve connection leading into his brain.
Although he retained full muscular function, he was completely trapped inside his own mind.
Through one-way glass, researchers monitored his slurred speech into a microphone.
On day four, he whispered that he heard hushed, unintelligible voices in his head.
Two days later, he began to weep, crying out that his dead wife was speaking to him.
Then, he began reciting the private names and secrets of the scientists' own dead relatives.
Terrified by what they had unsealed, half of the research team fled the facility that night.
Within a week, the whispers turned into a deafening roar of hundreds of spirits.
The man slammed himself against walls seeking pain, then begged for sedatives to sleep.
But in his dreams, he could see the dead circling him.
He clawed at his useless eyes, screaming that the voices spoke only of hell.
For five straight hours, he shrieked: No heaven, no forgiveness!
The scientists refused to stop, convinced they were moments away from contacting God.
Driven to absolute madness, he began thrashing violently until researchers strapped him down.
For two weeks, he stared blankly at the ceiling as silent tears ran down his face, kept alive only by intravenous fluids.
On the fifteenth night, the blind man slowly turned his head and made dead-center eye contact with the lead scientist through the glass.
He whispered: I have spoken with God, and he has abandoned us.
In that exact second, his heart stopped forever.
Would you have severed every sensory nerve to hear the voice of God?
